name: Congenital Varicella Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Virological Diagnosis of Congenital Varicella Syndrome

criteria.description: Maternal varicella infection during the first or early second trimester of pregnancy
Presence of characteristic congenital malformations including limb hypoplasia, cutaneous scarring, and ocular abnormalities
Detection of varicella-zoster virus DNA or antibodies in infant or fetal tissues
Neurological manifestations such as microcephaly or cortical atrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Maternal varicella infection during early pregnancy plus presence of at least two characteristic congenital anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by maternal history and virological testing when available.

laboratory: Varicella-zoster virus IgM antibodies in neonatal serum
PCR detection of VZV DNA in amniotic fluid or fetal tissues
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing limb hypoplasia and growth restriction
MRI brain demonstrating cortical atrophy and microcephaly
Ophthalmologic imaging revealing microphthalmia and chorioretinitis
genetic: No specific genetic mutation; diagnosis based on viral teratogenicity
other: Maternal history of varicella infection during first or early second trimester

distinguishingFeatures: Facial dysmorphism distinct from varicella scarring
No limb hypoplasia or dermatomal scarring

redFlags: Maternal varicella infection during first 20 weeks of gestation
Presence of limb hypoplasia with dermatomal skin scarring
Severe neurological impairment including microcephaly and seizures
references: Enders G, Miller E. Varicella-zoster virus infection in pregnancy. J Infect. 2010;60(6):423-434.
Pavlova M, et al. Congenital varicella syndrome: clinical and virological diagnosis. Clin Infect Dis. 2017;65(2):300-306.
